<objective>
Build the hermetic test harness the rest of the phase is verified against: a fake `claude` executable
that emits realistic `stream-json` NDJSON on demand, plus the one real-CLI probe that closes
RESEARCH.md's Open Question 2 before model routing is implemented.

Purpose: QUAL-02's integration tests must run in the default `npm test` with no real CLI, no auth, and
no billing. RESEARCH.md verified mechanically that `child_process.spawn()`'s bare-command resolution
honors `options.env.PATH` rather than the calling process's own `PATH`, which makes a fixture-on-PATH
approach fully hermetic — no global environment mutation, no cleanup step, no cross-test races under
`fileParallelism: false`.

Output: `src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/` with seven named scenarios, and a version-stamped
answer to "does `--model` accept the bare alias `sonnet`?".
</objective>

  <action>
Create the directory `src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/` containing three files.

**`claude`** — an executable Node script (shebang `#!/usr/bin/env node`, `chmod 0755`, no file
extension so it resolves as a bare `claude` command). It reads the scenario name from the
`FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO` environment variable, defaulting to `happy-path` when unset. It writes the
scenario's lines to stdout as NDJSON — one `JSON.stringify` per object, one object per line, each
terminated with `\n` — and exits with the scenario's declared exit code. It must also write its own
received argv, one JSON array, to the path named by `FLEET_FIXTURE_ARGV_OUT` when that variable is set,
so argv-contract tests (plan 02-04) can read back exactly what Fleet passed without parsing stdout.
Before exiting it must await the stdout drain callback, so a fast exit cannot truncate the last line.

**`scenarios.ts`** — a plain TypeScript module exporting a `FIXTURE_SCENARIOS` record keyed by scenario
name. Import the shapes from `../stream-events.js` rather than re-declaring them; do not invent
idealized shapes. The seven scenarios are:

- `happy-path` — `system/init`, one `assistant` line, then `result` with `subtype: 'success'` and
  `num_turns: 3`; exit code 0.
- `hang` — `system/init`, then spawn a detached grandchild that sleeps 300 seconds, print one
  `assistant` line, then block indefinitely without exiting. Never prints a `result` line. This is the
  scenario RUN-03's wall-clock cap and RUN-04's process-group kill are tested against, and the
  grandchild is what proves the whole group was reaped rather than just the direct child.
- `malformed-line` — `system/init`, then `MALFORMED_JSON_STRING`, then `BARE_STRING_LINE`, then a valid
  `assistant` line, then `result`/`success`; exit 0. Proves a malformed line is skipped rather than fatal.
- `unknown-event` — `system/init`, then `UNDOCUMENTED_TYPE_EVENT`, then `INVENTED_TYPE_EVENT`, then
  `result`/`success`; exit 0. Proves unknown `type` values are forward-compatible no-ops.
- `rate-limit` — `system/init`, then `RATE_LIMIT_EVENT_REJECTED`, then `API_RETRY_RATE_LIMIT`, then
  `result` with `subtype: 'error_during_execution'`; exit code 1.
- `api-key-source-leak` — a `system/init` line whose `apiKeySource` is the string `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
  instead of `none`, followed by an `assistant` line and a `result`; exit 0. This is what plan 02-06's
  D-02 assertion is tested against: the runner must kill the session on the init line and never reach the
  `assistant` line.
- `nonzero-exit` — `system/init`, one `assistant` line, no `result` line; exit code 143 (the
  documented SIGTERM code).

`stream-events.ts` currently exports a `SYSTEM_INIT_EVENT` with no `apiKeySource` field. Add
`apiKeySource: 'none'` to it — every real `system/init` line observed in Phase 1's captured evidence
carried this field with the value `none` under subscription auth, and the whole D-02 guarantee reads it,
so a fixture without it is not realistic. Add a sibling `SYSTEM_INIT_EVENT_LEAKED_KEY` export with
`apiKeySource: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'` for the `api-key-source-leak` scenario. Do not remove or renumber any
existing export — `src/spikes/rate-limit-classifier.test.ts` imports from this file and must stay green.

**`index.ts`** — exports `FAKE_CLAUDE_BIN_DIR`, the absolute path to `src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/`
resolved from `import.meta.url` (never from `process.cwd()`), and a `fixtureEnvFor(scenario)` helper
returning `{ FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO: scenario }` for callers to merge into a worker env. Also export the
`FixtureScenario` union type so a test cannot pass an unknown scenario name as a bare string.

Note for the executor: the fixture `claude` file has no `.test.ts` suffix, so Vitest's `unit` project
glob `src/**/*.test.ts` will not pick it up. Do not modify `vitest.config.ts` for this.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>test -x src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude &amp;&amp; FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO=happy-path ./src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude -p hi | tail -1 | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',d=>s+=d).on('end',()=>{const o=JSON.parse(s);if(o.type!=='result'||o.subtype!=='success'||o.num_turns!==3){process.exit(1)}console.log('OK')})"</automated>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>
    - `test -x src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude` succeeds (the file is executable, mode 0755).
    - `FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO=happy-path ./src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude -p hi` exits 0 and its last stdout line parses as JSON with `type === 'result'`, `subtype === 'success'`, `num_turns === 3`.
    - `FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO=nonzero-exit ./src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude -p hi; echo $?` prints `143`.
    - `FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO=api-key-source-leak ./src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude -p hi | head -1` parses as JSON whose `apiKeySource` field is the string `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
    - `FLEET_FIXTURE_SCENARIO=happy-path ./src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/claude -p hi | head -1` parses as JSON whose `apiKeySource` field is the string `none`.
    - `src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli/index.ts` exports `FAKE_CLAUDE_BIN_DIR` as an absolute path derived from `import.meta.url`.
    - `npm test -- src/spikes/rate-limit-classifier.test.ts` still exits 0 after the `stream-events.ts` additions.
    - `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>Seven named scenarios emit realistic NDJSON from an executable named `claude`, resolvable via a caller-supplied `PATH`.</done>
</task>

    - After `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM')`, both `process.kill(child.pid, 0)` and `process.kill(grandchildPid, 0)` throw an error with `code === 'ESRCH'` within 2 seconds.

  <action>
Create `src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli.test.ts` in the default `unit` project (a plain `.test.ts`,
NOT a `.spike.test.ts` — it spawns no real CLI and needs no auth). Cover every `<behavior>` case above.

For the grandchild-reaping assertion, spawn with `{ detached: true, shell: false, stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] }`
and kill with the negative-PID form `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM')` — RESEARCH.md Pattern 4
verified this exact shape terminates both the direct child and a backgrounded grandchild on this Linux
box. Use `process.kill(pid, 0)` as a no-op existence probe and assert the thrown error's `code` is
`ESRCH`; do not assert on the error message text, which is platform-dependent.

Assert hermeticity positively: read `process.env.PATH` inside the test and assert it does NOT include
`FAKE_CLAUDE_BIN_DIR`. This is the load-bearing property — if a future refactor reaches for `vi.stubEnv`
or a global `PATH` mutation, this assertion is what catches it before two tests race on shared state.

Give the kill-and-reap test an explicit timeout well above the 2-second reap window (10 seconds) so a
slow CI box does not produce a flake, and always clean up by attempting `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL')`
in a `finally` block wrapped in try/catch.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>npm test -- src/spikes/fixtures/fake-claude-cli.test.ts</automated>
  </verify>

  <action>
Create `src/spikes/model-alias.spike.test.ts` — an opt-in, real-CLI probe in the `spike` Vitest project
(the `.spike.test.ts` suffix is what excludes it from `npm test`). It resolves RESEARCH.md's Open
Question 2: CLAUDE.md §A1 states `--model` accepts the bare aliases `sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku`, but this
was never re-probed against the installed 2.1.218, and `tasks.model` already defaults to the literal
string `sonnet` — so plan 02-08's model routing (D-12) would be built on an unconfirmed assumption.

The probe runs `claude -p "hi" --model sonnet --output-format json --max-turns 1 --setting-sources ""`
inside a scratch repo (use `withScratchRepo` from `src/spikes/scratch-repo.ts` — never run a real-CLI
probe inside a registered project or inside the Fleet repository itself), asserts exit code 0, parses
the JSON result, and asserts a `modelUsage` key is present whose key names contain the substring
`sonnet`. Repeat for `haiku`. Do NOT probe `opus` — it is the most expensive tier and one alias
confirming plus one cheaper alias confirming is sufficient evidence that bare aliases resolve.

Record the finding via the existing findings-writer so the result is version-stamped with
`claudeVersion()` alongside Phase 1's SPIKE-01…05 entries. Name the finding `SPIKE-06: bare model alias
acceptance`.

If the probe fails — that is, the CLI rejects the bare alias and requires a full dated name such as
`claude-haiku-4-5` — do NOT silently add a lookup table. Fail the probe loudly and record the observed
error, so plan 02-08 is replanned around an alias-to-full-name adapter rather than shipping a broken
`--model` value. Assumption A4 is what this probe converts into a fact.
  </action>

  </verify>
